export interface Address {
  name: string
  email: string
}

export type AttachmentKind =
  | 'image'
  | 'pdf'
  | 'doc'
  | 'sheet'
  | 'slide'
  | 'zip'
  | 'code'
  | 'audio'
  | 'video'
  | 'other'

export interface Attachment {
  id: string
  name: string
  size: number
  kind: AttachmentKind
  /** Optional inline preview: an image data URL, or plain text for code/doc previews. */
  previewText?: string
  previewImage?: string
}

export interface Message {
  id: string
  threadId: string
  from: Address
  to: Address[]
  cc: Address[]
  bcc: Address[]
  /** ISO timestamp. */
  date: string
  /** Sanitized HTML fragment. */
  bodyHtml: string
  attachments: Attachment[]
  read: boolean
  starred: boolean
  /** True when the account owner sent it. */
  outgoing: boolean
  /** Set for messages queued by "Schedule send" that have not left the outbox. */
  scheduledFor?: string
}

export type Category = 'primary' | 'social' | 'promotions' | 'updates' | 'forums'

/** System labels double as folders, matching Gmail's model. */
export const SYSTEM = {
  inbox: 'INBOX',
  sent: 'SENT',
  trash: 'TRASH',
  spam: 'SPAM',
  important: 'IMPORTANT',
  scheduled: 'SCHEDULED',
} as const

export interface Thread {
  id: string
  subject: string
  messageIds: string[]
  labelIds: string[]
  category: Category
  /** ISO timestamp; while set the thread lives in Snoozed and leaves the inbox list. */
  snoozedUntil?: string
  muted?: boolean
}

export interface LabelColor {
  bg: string
  fg: string
}

export interface Label {
  id: string
  name: string
  color: LabelColor
  /** Shown in the sidebar's top section. */
  favorite?: boolean
}

export type ComposeMode = 'new' | 'reply' | 'replyAll' | 'forward'

export interface Draft {
  id: string
  threadId?: string
  inReplyTo?: string
  mode: ComposeMode
  to: Address[]
  cc: Address[]
  bcc: Address[]
  subject: string
  bodyHtml: string
  attachments: Attachment[]
  updatedAt: string
  scheduledFor?: string
}

export interface Contact extends Address {
  id: string
  title?: string
  company?: string
  /** Higher ranks first in autocomplete. */
  rank: number
}

export interface Account {
  name: string
  email: string
  avatarColor: string
  usedBytes: number
  quotaBytes: number
}

export interface MailData {
  version: number
  account: Account
  messages: Record<string, Message>
  threads: Record<string, Thread>
  drafts: Record<string, Draft>
  labels: Label[]
  contacts: Contact[]
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*  Views                                                                      */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

export type ViewId =
  | 'inbox'
  | 'starred'
  | 'snoozed'
  | 'important'
  | 'sent'
  | 'scheduled'
  | 'drafts'
  | 'all'
  | 'spam'
  | 'trash'

export interface ViewMeta {
  id: ViewId
  title: string
  icon: string
  /** Empty-state copy. */
  emptyTitle: string
  emptySubtitle: string
}

export type Density = 'default' | 'comfortable' | 'compact'
export type Theme = 'light' | 'dark' | 'system'
export type ReadingPane = 'none' | 'right'

export interface Settings {
  theme: Theme
  density: Density
  readingPane: ReadingPane
  conversationView: boolean
  showCategoryTabs: boolean
  undoSendSeconds: number
  signature: string
  signatureEnabled: boolean
  keyboardShortcuts: boolean
  pageSize: number
  markAsReadDelayMs: number
  hoverActions: boolean
  sendAndArchive: boolean
  previewText: boolean
  starClicked: boolean
}

import type { Category } from '@/lib/types' import type { PersonKey } from './people' export interface SeedAttachment { name: string /** Bytes. */ size: number text?: string } export interface SeedMessage { from: PersonKey to?: PersonKey[] cc?: PersonKey[] /** Minutes before "now". */ ago: number body: string read?: boolean starred?: boolean att?: SeedAttachment[] } export interface SeedThread { subject: string cat?: Category labels?: string[] box?: 'inbox' | 'archive' | 'trash' | 'spam' important?: boolean /** Minutes in the future. */ snooze?: number msgs: SeedMessage[] } const H = 60 const D = 1440 const sig = (name: string, role: string) => `

${name} · ${role} · Meridian

` const quote = (who: string, text: string) => `

${who} wrote:

${text}

` /* ========================================================================== */ /* Inbox — Primary */ /* ========================================================================== */ const primary: SeedThread[] = [ { subject: 'Design review: inbox density and the new label chips', labels: ['lb-work'], important: true, msgs: [ { from: 'priya', to: ['me'], cc: ['luis', 'design'], ago: 38, read: false, att: [ { name: 'inbox-density-v4.pdf', size: 2_842_112 }, { name: 'label-chips.png', size: 486_233 }, ], body: `

Avery —

I did another pass on row density last night and I think we finally have it. The short version: 44px rows with a 14px sender column reads better than anything else we tried, and it survives at 320px because the date column collapses instead of the subject.

Three things I want your read on before Thursday:

  1. The label chips now sit inline after the subject rather than trailing the snippet. It costs us ~60px of snippet on narrow screens but it stops the "where did my labels go" complaints.
  2. Unread rows use weight instead of a dot. Cleaner, but it leans on the font a lot — worth checking on Windows.
  3. I killed the hover background on the checkbox column. It was fighting the row hover.

PDF attached with all three side by side. The PNG is just the chip states if you want to drop them straight into the component.

${sig('Priya Raghavan', 'Head of Design')}`, }, { from: 'me', to: ['priya'], cc: ['luis', 'design'], ago: 26, body: `

This is a big improvement. 44px feels right — dense without the "spreadsheet" feeling we had in v2.

On (1): agreed, keep them inline. I'd add a rule that we never render more than two chips before collapsing to "+N", otherwise a thread with five labels eats the whole row.

On (2): I'll check Windows this afternoon. If it's shaky I'd rather add a 6px accent bar on the left edge than bring the dot back.

On (3): 👍

`, }, { from: 'priya', to: ['me'], cc: ['luis', 'design'], ago: 12, read: false, body: `

"+N" is right, I'll spec it. And yes to the accent bar over the dot — that also gives us somewhere to put the "important" marker without another glyph.

Thursday 2pm still good?

${quote('Avery Chen', 'This is a big improvement. 44px feels right…')}`, }, ], }, { subject: 'Search indexing is 4× slower after the storage migration', labels: ['lb-work', 'lb-follow'], important: true, msgs: [ { from: 'tom', to: ['me', 'jae'], ago: 5 * H, body: `

Heads up before you see the dashboards: full reindex went from 41 minutes to about 2h50m after we moved to the new storage layer. Nothing is on fire — incremental indexing is fine — but a cold rebuild is now a scary operation.

I bisected it to the batch reader. We're doing one round trip per document instead of per page.

// before: 1 fetch per 500 docs
// after:  1 fetch per doc  ← this
for (const id of ids) await store.get(id)

Fix is small. The annoying part is that our benchmark only ever measured incremental, so CI was green the whole way.

`, }, { from: 'jae', to: ['tom', 'me'], ago: 4 * H + 20, body: `

Confirmed on my side — p99 read latency on the index workers is 6ms, so it's pure round-trip count, not the storage layer being slow.

I can put a cold-rebuild benchmark in the nightly job. It's 3 hours of compute a night, which is fine.

`, }, { from: 'me', to: ['tom', 'jae'], ago: 3 * H, body: `

Nightly is worth it. Let's also add an alert if a rebuild crosses 60 minutes so we notice the next one within a day instead of a quarter.

Tom — do you want to land the batch fix, or should I? I have Thursday morning free.

`, }, { from: 'tom', to: ['me', 'jae'], ago: 2 * H + 5, read: false, att: [{ name: 'reindex-flamegraph.svg', size: 1_204_882 }], body: `

I'll take it, it's ~30 lines. Flamegraph attached for posterity — the whole right half of that chart is round trips.

One thing I want to flag: the fix restores the 41-minute number but I think we can get under 20 if we parallelize by shard. Not urgent, just noting it so we don't forget there's headroom.

${quote('Avery Chen', "Nightly is worth it. Let's also add an alert if a rebuild crosses 60 minutes…")}`, }, ], }, { subject: 'Q3 board deck — I need your slide by Thursday', labels: ['lb-work', 'lb-follow'], important: true, msgs: [ { from: 'dana', to: ['me'], cc: ['luis'], ago: 3 * H + 40, read: false, starred: true, att: [{ name: 'Q3-board-deck-draft.key', size: 18_442_311 }], body: `

Avery,

Board is Tuesday the 4th. I need one slide from you: what shipped in Q3 and what it moved. One slide. Not three.

The framing I'm using for the rest of the deck is "we got faster at the boring parts so we could spend the quarter on search." If your slide can land that, it'll do a lot of work for me.

Numbers I'd love if you have them:

  • Median time-to-first-result, before and after
  • Reindex duration (I hear this got worse — say so, boards trust people who volunteer bad news)
  • Anything on support ticket volume for search complaints

Draft deck attached so you can match the format. Thursday EOD, please — I write the narration Friday.

— D

This week: why the teams shipping fastest are usually running the least interesting stack.

I spent the last month talking to engineering leaders at eleven companies about their platform decisions. The pattern that emerged was uncomfortable for anyone who enjoys technology: the teams with the highest deploy frequency were, almost without exception, running the most conventional infrastructure available to them.

Not because boring is virtuous. Because novel infrastructure spends your debugging budget, and debugging budget is the scarcest resource an engineering team has. When your queue is the same queue ten thousand other companies run, your weird production incident has already been written up by someone else.

The counter-argument I got most often, and I think it's a fair one: sometimes the boring option genuinely cannot do the thing. The test I'd propose is whether you can articulate the specific limit you're hitting, in numbers. "It won't scale" is not that. "We're at 40,000 writes per second and the ceiling is 50,000" is.

Read the full issue · Unsubscribe

`, }, ], }, { subject: 'The attention economy has a supply problem', cat: 'updates', labels: ['lb-reading'], msgs: [ { from: 'stratechery', to: ['me'], ago: 6 * D + 14 * H, body: `

For twenty years the strategic question in consumer software was how to capture attention. The assumption underneath — that attention was abundant and the constraint was your ability to grab it — has quietly stopped being true.

The evidence is in the numbers nobody wants to headline: time spent per user is flat or declining across every major platform, while the number of things competing for that time keeps climbing. When supply is fixed and demand rises, you get an auction. That's what the last two years of feed products have been.

What this changes strategically: products that save time are, for the first time in a while, structurally advantaged over products that consume it. This is a reversal of the last decade's logic and most incumbents are organizationally incapable of acting on it, because their metrics are built the other way around.

Continue reading

This week: why the teams shipping fastest are usually running the least interesting stack.

I spent the last month talking to engineering leaders at eleven companies about their platform decisions. The pattern that emerged was uncomfortable for anyone who enjoys technology: the teams with the highest deploy frequency were, almost without exception, running the most conventional infrastructure available to them.

Not because boring is virtuous. Because novel infrastructure spends your debugging budget, and debugging budget is the scarcest resource an engineering team has. When your queue is the same queue ten thousand other companies run, your weird production incident has already been written up by someone else.

The counter-argument I got most often, and I think it's a fair one: sometimes the boring option genuinely cannot do the thing. The test I'd propose is whether you can articulate the specific limit you're hitting, in numbers. "It won't scale" is not that. "We're at 40,000 writes per second and the ceiling is 50,000" is.

Read the full issue · Unsubscribe

`, }, ], }, { subject: 'The attention economy has a supply problem', cat: 'updates', labels: ['lb-reading'], msgs: [ { from: 'stratechery', to: ['me'], ago: 6 * D + 14 * H, body: `

For twenty years the strategic question in consumer software was how to capture attention. The assumption underneath — that attention was abundant and the constraint was your ability to grab it — has quietly stopped being true.

The evidence is in the numbers nobody wants to headline: time spent per user is flat or declining across every major platform, while the number of things competing for that time keeps climbing. When supply is fixed and demand rises, you get an auction. That's what the last two years of feed products have been.

What this changes strategically: products that save time are, for the first time in a while, structurally advantaged over products that consume it. This is a reversal of the last decade's logic and most incumbents are organizationally incapable of acting on it, because their metrics are built the other way around.

Continue reading

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

The user gave a single task prompt (verbatim key constraints preserved):

- `<challenge>`: "Design and build the strongest Gmail-inspired email application you can. Recreate the clarity, information density, speed, and familiar workflows of a great modern inbox. Take the implementation as far as you can: choose the stack, scope, visual direction, data model, and technical limits that let you deliver the most convincing complete product."

- `<essential-outcomes>` — the finished app must include: a polished responsive mail shell (inbox, navigation, toolbar, search, account controls); a realistic seeded mailbox (varied senders, subjects, timestamps, labels, read states, attachments, threads, message content); functional navigation for at least Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts, Trash; working message selection, read/unread, starring, archiving, deleting, labeling; usable search; message-reading view with clear conversation hierarchy and useful actions; compose with recipients, subject, body, draft behavior, send behavior, polished interaction model; responsive on desktop and mobile.

- `<product-depth>`: "Go beyond a static visual recreation. Interactions should update the interface consistently, preserve state where useful, and make the product feel alive. You may add keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, category tabs, snoozing, scheduled mail, contact suggestions, rich composition, settings, themes, offline persistence, or any other details... No external email account, authentication, paid service, or API key is required. A fully local product with excellent seeded data and convincing behavior is valid. Do not leave prominent controls as decorative placeholders when a meaningful local interaction can be implemented."

- `<creative-freedom>`: "Do not explain your design before building it. Make the product and engineering decisions yourself, implement the experience, test the important workflows, and refine it into the best result you can."

- `<success-criteria>`: "The result should immediately read as a high-quality email client, reward exploration, and support a convincing end-to-end flow from finding a message to reading, organizing, composing, and sending mail. 38	function joinPeople(names: string[]) {
39	  if (names.length <= 3) return names.join(', ')
40	  return `${names[0]}, ${names[1]} .. ${names[names.length - 1]}`

43	export function summarize(
44	  thread: Thread,
45	  data: MailData,
46	  labelById: Map<string, Label>,
47	  draftByThread: Map<string, string>,
48	): ThreadSummary {
49	  const me = data.account.email
50	  const messages = thread.messageIds
51	    .map((id) => data.messages[id])
52	    .filter(Boolean)
53	    .sort((a, b) => Date.parse(a.date) - Date.parse(b.date))
54	
55	  const last = messages[messages.length - 1]
56	  const senderNames: string[] = []
57	  const recipientNames: string[] = []
58	  for (const m of messages) {
59	    const s = shortName(m.from, me)
60	    if (!senderNames.includes(s)) senderNames.push(s)
61	    for (const r of m.to) {
62	      const n = shortName(r, me)
63	      if (n !== 'me' && !recipientNames.includes(n)) recipientNames.push(n)
64	    }
65	  }
66	
67	  const attachmentNames = messages.flatMap((m) => m.attachments.map((a) => a.name))
68	
69	  return {
70	    id: thread.id,
71	    subject: thread.subject,
72	    snippet: last ? truncate(htmlToText(last.bodyHtml), 220) : '',
73	    messages,
74	    count: messages.length,
75	    date: last?.date ?? new Date(0).toISOString(),
76	    unread: messages.some((m) => !m.read),
77	    starred: messages.some((m) => m.starred),
78	    important: thread.labelIds.includes(SYSTEM.important),
79	    hasAttachment: attachmentNames.length > 0,
80	    attachmentNames,
81	    userLabels: thread.labelIds
82	      .map((id) => labelById.get(id))
83	      .filter((l): l is Label => Boolean(l)),
84	    category: thread.category,
85	    snoozedUntil: thread.snoozedUntil,
86	    scheduledFor: messages.find((m) => m.scheduledFor)?.scheduledFor,
87	    draftId: draftByThread.get(thread.id),
88	    senders: joinPeople(senderNames),

94	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
95	/*  View predicates                                                            */
96	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
97	
98	const isIn = (t: Thread, l: string) => t.labelIds.includes(l)
99	
100	function hasStar(t: Thread, data: MailData) {
101	  return t.messageIds.some((id) => data.messages[id]?.starred)
102	}
103	
104	function hasSent(t: Thread, data: MailData) {
105	  return t.messageIds.some((id) => {
106	    const m = data.messages[id]
107	    return m?.outgoing && !m.scheduledFor
108	  })
109	}
110	
111	function isSnoozed(t: Thread, now: number) {
112	  return Boolean(t.snoozedUntil && Date.parse(t.snoozedUntil) > now)
113	}
114	
115	export function viewPredicate(view: ViewId, data: MailData, now: number) {
116	  switch (view) {
117	    case 'inbox':
118	      return (t: Thread) =>
119	        isIn(t, SYSTEM.inbox) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam) && !isSnoozed(t, now)
120	    case 'starred':
121	      return (t: Thread) => hasStar(t, data) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam)
122	    case 'snoozed':
123	      return (t: Thread) => isSnoozed(t, now) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash)
124	    case 'important':
125	      return (t: Thread) =>
126	        isIn(t, SYSTEM.important) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam)
127	    case 'sent':
128	      return (t: Thread) => hasSent(t, data) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam)
129	    case 'scheduled':
130	      return (t: Thread) => isIn(t, SYSTEM.scheduled) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash)
131	    case 'spam':
132	      return (t: Thread) => isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam)
133	    case 'trash':
134	      return (t: Thread) => isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash)
135	    case 'all':
136	      return (t: Thread) => !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam)
137	    case 'drafts':
138	      return () => false
139	  }
140	}
141	
142	export function labelPredicate(labelId: string) {
143	  return (t: Thread) =>
144	    t.labelIds.includes(labelId) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam)
145	}
146	
147	/** The scope a bare search runs over: everything except trash and spam. */
148	export function searchPredicate(q: Query, data: MailData, now: number) {
149	  const scope = queryScope(q)
150	  if (scope === 'anywhere') return () => true
151	  if (scope === 'default') return (t: Thread) => !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam)
152	  if (scope === 'drafts') return () => false
153	  return viewPredicate(scope as ViewId, data, now)
154	}

160	export interface Counts {
161	  inboxUnread: number
162	  inboxTotal: number
163	  starred: number
164	  snoozed: number
165	  important: number
166	  drafts: number
167	  scheduled: number
168	  spam: number
169	  trash: number
170	  sent: number
171	  byCategory: Record<Category, { total: number; unread: number }>
172	  byLabel: Record<string, { total: number; unread: number }>
173	}
174	
175	export function computeCounts(data: MailData, now: number): Counts {
176	  const byCategory = {
177	    primary: { total: 0, unread: 0 },
178	    social: { total: 0, unread: 0 },
179	    promotions: { total: 0, unread: 0 },
180	    updates: { total: 0, unread: 0 },
181	    forums: { total: 0, unread: 0 },
182	  } as Record<Category, { total: number; unread: number }>
183	  const byLabel: Record<string, { total: number; unread: number }> = {}
184	  for (const l of data.labels) byLabel[l.id] = { total: 0, unread: 0 }
185	
186	  const counts: Counts = {
187	    inboxUnread: 0,
188	    inboxTotal: 0,
189	    starred: 0,
190	    snoozed: 0,
191	    important: 0,
192	    drafts: Object.keys(data.drafts).length,
193	    scheduled: 0,
194	    spam: 0,
195	    trash: 0,
196	    sent: 0,
197	    byCategory,
198	    byLabel,
199	  }
200	
201	  const inbox = viewPredicate('inbox', data, now)
202	  for (const t of Object.values(data.threads)) {
203	    const unread = t.messageIds.some((id) => {
204	      const m = data.messages[id]
205	      return m && !m.read
206	    })
207	    if (inbox(t)) {
208	      counts.inboxTotal += 1
209	      if (unread) counts.inboxUnread += 1
210	      byCategory[t.category].total += 1
211	      if (unread) byCategory[t.category].unread += 1
212	    }
213	    if (isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash)) counts.trash += 1
214	    else if (isIn(t, SYSTEM.spam)) counts.spam += 1
215	    else {
216	      if (hasStar(t, data)) counts.starred += 1
217	      if (isSnoozed(t, now)) counts.snoozed += 1
218	      if (isIn(t, SYSTEM.important)) counts.important += 1
219	      if (hasSent(t, data)) counts.sent += 1
220	      for (const id of t.labelIds) {
221	        if (byLabel[id]) {
222	          byLabel[id].total += 1
223	          if (unread) byLabel[id].unread += 1
224	        }
225	      }
226	    }
227	    if (isIn(t, SYSTEM.scheduled) && !isIn(t, SYSTEM.trash)) counts.scheduled += 1
228	  }
229	  return counts
230	}

232	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
233	/*  List building                                                              */
234	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
235	
236	export interface ListRequest {
237	  view: ViewId
238	  labelId?: string
239	  searchText?: string
240	  category?: Category
241	  now: number
242	}
243	
244	export interface ListResult {
245	  threads: ThreadSummary[]
246	  drafts: Draft[]
247	  query: Query | null
248	}
249	
250	export function buildList(data: MailData, req: ListRequest): ListResult {
251	  const labelById = new Map(data.labels.map((l) => [l.id, l]))
252	  const labelsByName = new Map(data.labels.map((l) => [l.name.toLowerCase(), l]))
253	  const draftByThread = new Map<string, string>()
254	  for (const d of Object.values(data.drafts)) if (d.threadId) draftByThread.set(d.threadId, d.id)
255	
256	  const searchText = req.searchText?.trim()
257	  const query = searchText ? parseQuery(searchText, req.now) : null
258	
259	  let threads: Thread[]
260	  let drafts: Draft[] = []
261	
262	  if (query && !query.empty) {
263	    const scope = searchPredicate(query, data, req.now)
264	    threads = Object.values(data.threads).filter(
265	      (t) => scope(t) && matchesQuery(t, query, data, labelsByName),
266	    )
267	    drafts = Object.values(data.drafts).filter((d) => draftMatches(d, query, data))
268	  } else if (req.view === 'drafts') {
269	    threads = []
270	    drafts = Object.values(data.drafts)
271	  } else if (req.labelId) {
272	    const pred = labelPredicate(req.labelId)
273	    threads = Object.values(data.threads).filter(pred)
274	  } else {
275	    const pred = viewPredicate(req.view, data, req.now)
276	    threads = Object.values(data.threads).filter(pred)
277	    if (req.view === 'inbox' && req.category) {
278	      threads = threads.filter((t) => t.category === req.category)
279	    }
280	  }
281	
282	  const summaries = threads.map((t) => summarize(t, data, labelById, draftByThread))
283	
284	  if (req.view === 'scheduled' && !query) {
285	    summaries.sort((a, b) => Date.parse(a.scheduledFor ?? a.date) - Date.parse(b.scheduledFor ?? b.date))
286	  } else if (req.view === 'snoozed' && !query) {
287	    summaries.sort((a, b) => Date.parse(a.snoozedUntil ?? a.date) - Date.parse(b.snoozedUntil ?? b.date))
288	  } else {
289	    summaries.sort((a, b) => Date.parse(b.date) - Date.parse(a.date))
290	  }
291	
292	  drafts = [...drafts].sort((a, b) => Date.parse(b.updatedAt) - Date.parse(a.updatedAt))
293	
294	  return { threads: summaries, drafts, query }
295	}
296	
297	function draftMatches(d: Draft, q: Query, data: MailData) {
298	  if (q.in && q.in !== 'drafts' && q.in !== 'anywhere') return false
299	  if (q.isStarred || q.isImportant || q.isSnoozed || q.isRead) return false
300	  if (q.hasAttachment && !d.attachments.length) return false
301	  if (q.subject && !d.subject.toLowerCase().includes(q.subject)) return false
302	  if (q.from && q.from !== 'me' && !data.account.email.includes(q.from)) return false
303	  if (q.to && !d.to.some((a) => a.email.toLowerCase().includes(q.to!) || a.name.toLowerCase().includes(q.to!)))
304	    return false
305	  if (q.labelNames.length) return false
306	  const hay = `${d.subject} ${htmlToText(d.bodyHtml)} ${d.to.map((a) => `${a.name} ${a.email}`).join(' ')}`.toLowerCase()
307	  for (const t of q.terms) if (!hay.includes(t)) return false
308	  for (const p of q.phrases) if (!hay.includes(p)) return false
309	  return true
310	}

2	import type { Category, ViewId } from '@/lib/types'
3	
4	export interface Route {
5	  view: ViewId
6	  labelId?: string
7	  search?: string
8	  threadId?: string
9	  /** Settings tab id; the settings screen replaces the list when set. */
10	  settingsTab?: string
11	  category?: Category
12	}
13	
14	const VIEWS: ViewId[] = [
15	  'inbox',
16	  'starred',
17	  'snoozed',
18	  'important',
19	  'sent',
20	  'scheduled',
21	  'drafts',
22	  'all',
23	  'spam',
24	  'trash',
25	]
26	
27	export function parseHash(hash: string): Route {
28	  const raw = hash.replace(/^#\/?/, '')
29	  const [pathPart, queryPart] = raw.split('?')
30	  const params = new URLSearchParams(queryPart ?? '')
31	  const segments = pathPart.split('/').filter(Boolean).map(decodeURIComponent)
32	
33	  const route: Route = { view: 'inbox' }
34	  const head = segments[0]
35	
36	  if (head === 'settings') {
37	    route.settingsTab = segments[1] || 'general'
38	    return route
39	  }
40	  if (head === 'label' && segments[1]) {
41	    route.labelId = segments[1]
42	    route.view = 'all'
43	    route.threadId = segments[2]
44	  } else if (head === 'search') {
45	    route.view = 'all'
46	    route.search = params.get('q') ?? ''
47	    route.threadId = segments[1]
48	  } else if (head && (VIEWS as string[]).includes(head)) {
49	    route.view = head as ViewId
50	    route.threadId = segments[1]
51	  }
52	
53	  const cat = params.get('cat')
54	  if (cat) route.category = cat as Category
55	  return route
56	}
57	
58	export function serializeRoute(r: Route): string {
59	  if (r.settingsTab) return `#/settings/${r.settingsTab}`
60	  const params = new URLSearchParams()
61	  let path: string
62	  if (r.search !== undefined) {
63	    path = 'search'
64	    params.set('q', r.search)
65	  } else if (r.labelId) {
66	    path = `label/${encodeURIComponent(r.labelId)}`
67	  } else {
68	    path = r.view
69	  }
70	  if (r.threadId) path += `/${encodeURIComponent(r.threadId)}`
71	  if (r.category && r.view === 'inbox' && !r.search && !r.labelId) params.set('cat', r.category)
72	  const q = params.toString()
73	  return `#/${path}${q ? `?${q}` : ''}`
74	}
75	
76	export function useRouter() {
77	  const [route, setRoute] = useState<Route>(() => parseHash(window.location.hash))
78	
79	  useEffect(() => {
80	    const onChange = () => setRoute(parseHash(window.location.hash))
81	    window.addEventListener('hashchange', onChange)
82	    if (!window.location.hash) window.location.replace('#/inbox')
83	    return () => window.removeEventListener('hashchange', onChange)
84	  }, [])
85	
86	  const navigate = useCallback((next: Route, replace = false) => {
87	    const hash = serializeRoute(next)
88	    if (hash === window.location.hash) {
89	      setRoute(next)
90	      return
91	    }
92	    if (replace) window.history.replaceState(null, '', hash)
93	    else window.history.pushState(null, '', hash)
94	    setRoute(parseHash(hash))
95	  }, [])
96	
97	  const back = useCallback(() => window.history.back(), [])
98	
99	  return { route, navigate, back }
100	}

37	  const [toasts, setToasts] = useState<Toast[]>([])
38	  const timers = useRef(new Map<number, number>())
39	
40	  const dismiss = useCallback((id: number) => {
41	    setToasts((list) => list.filter((t) => t.id !== id))
42	    const timer = timers.current.get(id)

54	      setToasts((list) => {
55	        list.forEach((t) => {

57	          if (timer) window.clearTimeout(timer)

59	        })
60	        return [{ id, message, actions: opts?.actions ?? [], duration, createdAt: Date.now() }]

if (await reply.count()) {
  await reply.click()
  await page.waitForTimeout(600)
  log('compose windows after reply:', await page.locator('[data-compose]').count())
  await shot('03-reply')
  const discard = page.getByRole('button', { name: /discard/i }).first()
  if (await discard.count()) await discard.click()
  await page.waitForTimeout(300)
}

// ---- 3. back to list, keyboard shortcuts -----------------------------
await page.keyboard.press('u')
await page.waitForTimeout(400)
log('hash after u:', await page.evaluate(() => location.hash))
await page.keyboard.press('j')
await page.keyboard.press('j')
await page.keyboard.press('x')
await page.waitForTimeout(300)
await shot('04-selection')
await page.keyboard.press('e') // archive
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
const toast = await page.locator('text=/Undo|archived|Conversation/i').first().textContent().catch(() => null)
log('toast after archive:', toast)
await shot('05-archived-toast')
await page.keyboard.press('z') // undo
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
log('rows after undo:', await page.locator('ul > li').count())

// ---- 4. search --------------------------------------------------------
await page.keyboard.press('/')
await page.waitForTimeout(200)
await page.keyboard.type('is:unread has:attachment')
await page.keyboard.press('Enter')
await page.waitForTimeout(600)
log('hash after search:', await page.evaluate(() => location.hash))
log('search results:', await page.locator('ul > li').count())
await shot('06-search')

// ---- 5. compose + send ------------------------------------------------
await page.goto(URL + '#/inbox', { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForTimeout(400)
await page.getByRole('button', { name: /compose/i }).first().click()
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /^To$/i }).first().fill('mei')
await page.waitForTimeout(400)
await page.keyboard.press('Enter')
await page.getByPlaceholder(/subject/i).first().fill('Playwright verification note')
await page.locator('[contenteditable="true"]').last().click()
await page.keyboard.type('Checking the send + undo contract end to end.')
await shot('07-compose')
await page.getByRole('button', { name: /^Send$/ }).first().click()
await page.waitForTimeout(700)
log('toast after send:', await page.locator('text=/Message sent/i').first().textContent().catch(() => null))
await shot('08-sent-toast')
await page.goto(URL + '#/sent', { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForTimeout(600)
log('first sent row:', await page.locator('ul > li').first().innerText().catch(() => null))

// ---- 6. drafts / settings / dark --------------------------------------
await page.goto(URL + '#/settings/general', { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
await shot('09-settings')
await page.goto(URL + '#/inbox', { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForTimeout(300)
await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.classList.add('dark'))
await page.waitForTimeout(300)
await shot('10-dark')

// ---- 7. mobile ---------------------------------------------------------
const m = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 }, isMobile: true, hasTouch: true })
await m.goto(URL + '#/inbox', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' })
await m.waitForTimeout(700)
await m.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/11-mobile-list.png` })
await m.locator('ul > li').first().click()
await m.waitForTimeout(600)
await m.screenshot({ path: `${OUT}/12-mobile-thread.png` })

console.log('ERRORS:', JSON.stringify(errors, null, 2))
await browser.close()

# Claude Opus 5 — Mail

A local-first, Gmail-inspired email client. No backend, no accounts, no API keys: the
mailbox is seeded from hand-written data and every action is real, persisted to
`localStorage`, and undoable.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:9214
pnpm build      # tsc -b && vite build
pnpm preview    # http://localhost:9214
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
```

## What's in it

**Mail shell** — collapsible sidebar with live counts, icon rail at medium widths, drawer on
phones; category tabs (Primary / Promotions / Social / Updates / Forums); density,
reading-pane, and theme controls; light, dark and system themes.

**Views** — Inbox, Starred, Snoozed, Sent, Drafts, Scheduled, All mail, Spam, Trash,
Important, plus one view per user label.

**Data** — ~60 threads with multi-message conversations, quoted replies, HTML bodies,
attachments (with image thumbnails and text previews), 50 contacts, 8 labels, read/unread
and starred state, drafts, snoozed threads, and a scheduled send.

**Actions** — select (click, shift-range, or the select-all dropdown), star, mark
important, read/unread, archive, trash, restore, spam, label, move, snooze, mute, empty
trash/spam. Everything destructive raises a snackbar with **Undo**, which restores the
whole mailbox snapshot.

**Search** — full operator support: `from: to: subject: label: in: is: has: filename:
before: after: older_than: newer_than:` plus `"quoted phrases"`. Matches are highlighted in
the list. There's an advanced-search popover that builds the query for you, and recent
searches are remembered.

**Compose** — multiple stacked windows (minimize / pop out / full screen), contact
autocomplete with chips, Cc/Bcc, rich-text formatting, attachments read from disk,
signature, schedule send, and undo send. Drafts save as you type and survive reload.

**Reading** — collapsed message stack with expand-all, quoted text folded behind `···`,
per-message reply / reply-all / forward, attachment preview dialog, banners for scheduled,
snoozed, muted and spam threads.

**Keyboard** — `c` compose, `j`/`k` cursor, `Enter` open, `u` back, `x` select, `s` star,
`e` archive, `#` trash, `!` spam, `b` snooze, `r`/`a`/`f` reply/reply-all/forward,
`Shift+I`/`Shift+U` read/unread, `[`/`]` prev/next, `z` undo, `g` then `i s t d a`, `/`
search, `?` shortcut reference.

## Stack

Vite 8 · React 19 · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS v4 · immer · lucide-react. State lives in a
single reducer over an immer draft; the router is hash-based; persistence is a debounced,
versioned `localStorage` write.

## Expanding the Oxlint configuration

If you are developing a production application, we recommend enabling type-aware lint rules by installing `oxlint-tsgolint` and editing `.oxlintrc.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "plugins": ["react", "typescript", "oxc"],
  "options": {
    "typeAware": true
  },
  "rules": {
    "react/rules-of-hooks": "error",
    "react/only-export-components": ["warn", { "allowConstantExport": true }]
  }
}
```

See the [Oxlint rules documentation](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules) for the full list of rules and categories.

The build is complete.

**Claude Opus 5 — Mail**, a local-first Gmail-style client at `http://localhost:9214`.

**What it does**
- **Views:** Inbox, Starred, Snoozed, Important, Sent, Drafts, Scheduled, All mail, Spam, Trash, plus per-label views — all with live counts and category tabs (Primary/Promotions/Social/Updates/Forums).
- **Actions:** select (click, shift-range, select-all dropdown), star, important, read/unread, archive, trash, restore, spam, label, move, snooze, mute, empty trash. Destructive actions get a snackbar with **Undo** that restores a full mailbox snapshot.
- **Search:** `from: to: subject: label: in: is: has: filename: before: after: older_than: newer_than:` plus quoted phrases, with in-list match highlighting, an advanced-search builder, and recent searches.
- **Compose:** stacked windows (minimize / pop out / full screen), contact autocomplete with chips, Cc/Bcc, rich text, real file attachments, signature, schedule send, undo send; drafts autosave and survive reload.
- **Reading:** collapsed message stack, folded quoted text, per-message reply/reply-all/forward, attachment preview, banners for scheduled/snoozed/muted/spam.
- **Depth:** full keyboard model (`j/k`, `x`, `e`, `#`, `b`, `r/a/f`, `g`+`i s t d a`, `/`, `z`, `?`), settings with density / reading pane / preview / hover actions / page size, light–dark–system themes, and versioned `localStorage` persistence.

**Checks run:** `pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm lint` 0 errors (9 fast-refresh warnings on files that export both a provider and its hook) · `pnpm build` → 439.85 kB / 138.20 kB gzip · headless-browser pass over open/reply/archive/undo/search/compose/send/snooze/schedule/settings/dark/reload-persistence at 1440, 1024, 768 and 390 px, with 0 console or page errors.

Title and visible `<h1>` are both `Claude Opus 5`. Everything stayed inside the working directory; the dev server is still running on 9214.
